correctness.rationale: For an omitted vertex, the proof derives its multiset exactly from the omission sizes and whether its deleted matching mate is selected. This yields at most two types per shore, the exact intersection condition when two vertices are omitted from a shore, and explicit cross-shore collisions in both equal-size cases. The remaining five patterns are checked in both directions and counted. Direct breadth-first-search verification over every subset for \(3\le n\le8\) agrees exactly with the theorem; the finite check is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification on the canonical one-factor deletion of a balanced biclique, not an arbitrary finite slice. It determines the minimum, all minimum sets, and every resolving-set size. The exact comparison \(2n-1\to2n-3\) under deletion of one perfect matching and the absence of size \(2n-2\) resolving sets expose meaningful structure beyond a routine recomputation.
